chains.title: Risk T allele strengthens a GATA3-bound TOX3 enhancer

links.claim: GATA3 is occupied at the variant in MCF-7 (5 MCF-7 peaks, E21; E06) and is one of the most highly expressed TFs there (346 TPM, rank 5). No QBiC-SELEX model or direct allele-specific GATA3 assay is provided, so the proposal that the alt T allele strengthens GATA3 binding is an inference from T being the reported risk/effect allele, not a measured affinity change. Occupancy plus high expression favor GATA3 over other GATA-motif factors, but this remains correlational.
The variant lies inside EH38E3180851, a distal enhancer-like cCRE with DNase and H3K27ac marks, consistent with an active regulatory element.

TOX3 is the nearest protein-coding gene (17.5 kb upstream) and receives strong fine-mapping/L2G support as the target of this breast cancer signal. GTEx v8 shows no significant eQTL at this base, but those data are not from breast cancer cells and do not test this context.
MCF-7 is a luminal breast cancer line in which GATA3 is bound at this element and very highly expressed.
The locus is strongly associated with breast cancer, with the T allele reported as the effect allele in the strongest breast cancer associations; L2G links the credible set to TOX3.

predictions: The alt T allele improves the GATA3 motif score and shows stronger allele-specific GATA3 binding than C in MCF-7 cells.
CRISPR C>T increases enhancer activity and TOX3 expression in breast cancer cells, and GATA3 depletion reduces this effect.
falsified_if: Allele-specific GATA3 assays show equal or stronger binding on the C allele.
The C/T change does not alter enhancer activity or TOX3 expression in breast cancer cells.
GATA3 perturbation does not affect the enhancer or TOX3 expression.
Fine-mapping shows a different linked variant, not this base, is causal.

chains.title: Risk T allele strengthens a FOXA1-bound TOX3 enhancer

links.claim: FOXA1 is occupied at the variant in MCF-7 (8 MCF-7 peaks, E05) and expressed there (rank 28). No QBiC-SELEX model or direct allele-specific FOXA1 assay is provided, so the claim that the alt T allele strengthens FOXA1 binding is inferred from T being the reported risk allele and from occupancy, not measured. FOXA1 is a pioneer TF that can act with GATA3 at the same element.
The variant is in EH38E3180851, an active distal enhancer-like element marked by DNase and H3K27ac.
TOX3 is the nearest protein-coding gene and is the best-supported target from genetic fine-mapping/L2G. GTEx v8 lacks a significant eQTL here, but those tissues are not breast cancer cells.
MCF-7 breast cancer cells show FOXA1 ChIP occupancy at this element and express FOXA1.
This locus is a strong breast cancer susceptibility signal, with T reported as the effect allele in the strongest breast cancer GWAS associations.

predictions: The alt T allele improves the FOXA1 motif score and shows stronger allele-specific FOXA1 binding than C in MCF-7 cells.
FOXA1 depletion reduces T-allele enhancer activity and TOX3 expression.
falsified_if: FOXA1 binds equally to both alleles or preferentially to the C allele.
FOXA1 perturbation does not alter enhancer activity or TOX3 expression.
A different linked variant is shown to be causal.

chains.title: Null: no TF-mediated effect of this exact variant
predictions: No allele-specific TF binding at chr16:52565276 is found for a relevant breast cancer TF.
The GWAS signal is explained by a linked causal variant in the credible set rather than this base.
The C/T change does not alter enhancer activity or TOX3 expression in relevant breast cancer cells.
falsified_if: Allele-specific binding of a relevant TF at this exact base is demonstrated together with an enhancer/TOX3 expression effect.
CRISPR or reporter assays show the C/T change itself alters regulatory activity in breast cancer cells.

chains.title: Risk T allele strengthens an SPDEF-bound TOX3 enhancer

links.claim: SPDEF is occupied at the variant in MCF-7 (2 peaks, E07) and expressed (rank 40). No QBiC-SELEX model or direct allele-specific SPDEF assay is provided, so the proposal that the alt T allele strengthens SPDEF binding is inferred from the risk allele and occupancy, not measured. Occupancy support is weaker than for GATA3 or FOXA1.
The variant lies in an active distal enhancer-like cCRE, EH38E3180851.
TOX3 is the nearest protein-coding gene and receives strong L2G support as the target of the breast cancer signal.
SPDEF ChIP peaks containing the variant are present in MCF-7 cells, where SPDEF is expressed.
The variant is associated with breast cancer risk, with T the reported effect allele in major breast cancer GWAS.

predictions: SPDEF ChIP or binding is stronger on the T allele than the C allele at this element in MCF-7 cells.
SPDEF knockdown reduces T-allele enhancer activity or TOX3 expression.
falsified_if: SPDEF binding is not allele-specific at this base.
SPDEF perturbation does not affect the enhancer or TOX3 expression.
SPDEF occupancy is explained entirely by another factor at the element.

This leaves the link relying only on the indirect inference from T being the risk allele, leading to weak support.

checks.why: To establish if there are direct expression quantitative trait loci (eQTL) linking this variant (or linked variants) to TOX3 expression specifically in MCF7 (which is the context of all TF binding data), providing direct evidence for the regulatory consequence of the variant.

matrix.test: Depletion of GATA3 vs FOXA1 vs SPDEF in MCF-7, measuring TOX3 and T-allele enhancer activity

outcomes.outcome: GATA3 depletion reduces TOX3/enhancer activity; FOXA1 and SPDEF depletion do not.
FOXA1 depletion reduces TOX3/enhancer activity; GATA3 and SPDEF depletion do not.

next_experiment: Run the cheapest separating test first: compute ref/alt PWM scores for the GATA3 and FOXA1 motifs from the existing genomic sequence. If the alt T changes only one motif, that directly favors H1 or H2; if neither changes, proceed to allele-specific GATA3/FOXA1 ChIP or EMSA in MCF-7 cells.
